post.caption: Cartier's clock hands seem to float. Cartier calls them Mystery Clocks, and nothing seems to hold the hands. Maurice Couet built the first one for Louis Cartier, inspired by the French magician and clockmaker Robert Houdin. The secret is that the hands are fixed to two transparent discs of glass or crystal, and toothed edges connect them to gears hidden in the base. Between 1923 and 1925, Cartier made six Portico clocks shaped like Japanese gates. The first went to the opera singer Ganna Walska, and Cartier later bought it back. Since 1973, it has been kept in the Cartier Collection.
